chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Muni'a told us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn 'Arifah narrated to us, narrated 'Ali ibn Thabit, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Two groups of my nation have no share in Islam: the Marji'ah and the Qadariyyah.

key_terms.الْمُرْجِئَةُ: The Marji'ah (a theological group known for delaying judgment on sinners)
key_terms.وَالْقَدَرِيَّةُ: And the Qadariyyah (a theological group emphasizing human free will over divine decree)

ai.seo_question: Which two groups of people are said to have no share in Islam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the early Shia concern with theological orthodoxy by identifying the Marji'ah and Qadariyyah as the two groups excluded from true Islam. While the Marji'ah are often associated with excusing major sins through divine promise, the Qadariyyah here represent those who deny divine decree (Qadr) in favor of absolute human autonomy, a view Shia scholarship contrasts with the balance of *amr bayn al-amrayn* (affair between the two affairs). This classification underscores the importance of adhering to both divine predestination and human responsibility as core tenets of Islamic faith.
